messages:
alex: Heads-up  saw a recurring eviction spiral in ap-southeast1 this morning. Batch inference fleets kept getting preempted and re-scheduled across racks, ended up with a wave of Pending tiny pods.

 maria: yea spotted that, p99 token latency jumped ~300ms for the hosted route. Several small pods never recovered and got stuck Pending for 10+ mins.

 tyler: initial look: scheduler logs show repeated failed pack attempts then fallback to spreading. I think preferredDuringScheduling anti-affinity + rack taints prevented consolidation.

 alex: logs: 
```
I0321 07:12:03.123 kube-scheduler] Scheduling pod inference-small-24: failed to fit 3/5 nodes: NodeAffinity mismatch, Taint:NoSchedule present on rack-13, PreferredAffinity conflict
I0321 07:12:05.456 eviction-controller] Preempting pod inference-small-17 for higher priority job, reschedule attempt 4
```

 mina: we also saw a conntrack burst on rack-13 around the same time per net-metrics. That probably slowed kubelet heartbeats and made the scheduler conservative.

 kevin: can we confirm which component did the preempting? scheduler vs preemption controller?

 tyler: preemption comes from kube-scheduler scoring -> preemptor. But our custom taint-based fallback heuristics in the descheduler ran shortly after and caused a chain: pack->fail->spread->deschedule->preempt.

 maria: cost hit note: during the window we used ~42 extra GPU-hours (estimate) vs baseline. Rough $420/day delta if sustained. Not huge but recurring spikes add up.

 alex: hypothesis: fractional GPU requests + preferred anti-affinity rule causes the scheduler to avoid packing small pods on already-used rack nodes. When hot-net/conntrack makes nodes appear slow, the scheduler backs off and starts moving pods, amplifying fragmentation.

 tyler: proposal: two-phase experiment today: 1) temporarily relax preferred anti-affinity for inference-small (preferred -> weight 10 -> 2) 2) enable binpack-mode=consolidate on a single AZ (ap-southeast1a) and run for 2 hours, 3) increase descheduler cooldown to reduce churn.

 mina: I’ll run a simulation first against the replay cluster with 2h of trace (traffic from 07:00-09:00) and post diff. If results look good, roll to canary.

 kevin: what about safety? If we consolidate, risk of single-rack failure impact increases. Need to keep rack-level replica spread for stateful things, but stateless inference can be denser. 

 maria: agreed  add a service-level label to opt-in for consolidation: "consolidate-safe=true" and only apply to that class.

 alex: ops plan: Mina runs sim at 15:00 UTC, Tyler will prepare scheduler config patch, Maria will estimate cost delta if consolidation is left on for a week. Aim to revert in 4 hours if p99 or error rate regresses.

 deploy-bot: CI job #8234 started: cluster-replay-sim (trace=ap-southeast1-07-09, config=consolidate-experiment). Link: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/8234

 mina: sim started. Ill attach profiler and the scheduler trace. Expect initial output in ~25m.

 tyler: also adding a small tweak: reduce preemption aggressiveness by lowering preemptionThreshold from 0.9 -> 0.8 for low-priority pods during the canary window. That should stop the rapid evict->reschedule loop.

 alex: good. If sim shows <1% extra latency and >25% reduction in evictions, we can roll canary. Keep alerts for evictions/sec and p99_generation_latency.

 maria: noted. Creating a dashboard widget and an alert runbook entry.

 mina: sim results posted: eviction count down 48%, consolidated GPU usage up 6%, p99 latency +80ms. Attaching scheduler trace and sim-summary in the CI artifact.

 tyler: 80ms p99 regression might be acceptable for hosted non-PL customers but not our strict SLA tiers. Suggest: only enable consolidation for non-SLA or dedicated fleets and keep default scheduling for SLA routes.

 kevin: decision: adopt opt-in label for consolidation; add an autoscale margin to absorb node loss (reserve 5% headroom). Create PR for scheduler config + classification label.

 alex: action items: Mina PR with sim logs (in flight), Tyler PR for scheduler tweaks, Maria PR for dashboard and cost calc, Kevin to coordinate rollout policy. Targeting deploy canary tomorrow at 09:00 UTC.

 maria: thanks all  tracking in #incidents as follow-up. :white_check_mark:
